MARATHA STATE (1674-1720) AND MARATHA CONFIDERCY (1720-1818)

Shivaji (1674-1680)

  • Born at: Shivneri Fort in 1630.
  • Father: Shahji Bhonsle.
  • Mother: Jija Bai.
  • Religious teacher: Samarth Ramdas.

Expeditions of Shivaji

#### Battle of Pratapgarh (1659)

  • The battle was fought between the Maratha forces led by Shivaji and the Bijapur troops under General Afzal Khan, representing Adil Shah.
  • The Marathas emerged victorious.
  • Shaista Khan (Governor of Deccan) was deputed by Aurangzeb to put down rising power of Shivaji in 1660 (Shivaji lost Poona but later made a bold attack against him in 1663 and plundered Surat (1664) and later Ahmadnagar).

#### Treaty of Purandar (1665)

  • In 1665 AD, Aurangzeb appointed Raja Jai Singh I of Amber to lead a campaign against Shivaji, resulting in the Treaty of Purandar. Shivaji agreed to give his 23 out of total 35 Forts to Mughals.
  • In 1665 AD, Shivaji visited Aurangzeb's court in Agra, where he was imprisoned but managed to escape the same year.
  • In 1674 AD, Shivaji proclaimed himself "Chhatrapati" at his coronation ceremony held at Raigad Fort.
  • Shivaji was considered a pioneer of Guerilla warfare.
  • He captured Torana Fort at the age of 16.
  • Shivaji was helped by the Ashtapradhan (eight ministers).

Revenue Sources

  • Marathas conducted raids and extracted Chauth, which was 1/4th of the land revenue.
  • Sardeshmukhi was an additional tax of 10% tax imposed on top of the regular revenue collection (Chauth).

Sambhaji (1681-1689)

  • He was the eldest son of Shivaji and Saibai.
  • He defeated Rajaram, his younger brother in the war of succession.
  • He also provided protection and support to Mirza Akbar, the rebellious son of Aurangzeb due to which he gave gruesome death to Sambhaji.

Rajaram (1689-1700)

  • He was the son of Shivaji and Soyarabai.
  • He succeeded the throne with the help of ministers at Rajgarh.
  • He created a new post: Pratinidhi [Total no. of minister now nine (Pratinidhi + Ashtapradhan)].
  • He died in Satara which became the capital after the fall of Jinji to Mughal (1698).

Tarabai

  • She was the wife of Rajaram.
  • Son: Shivaji II.

Shahuji (1708-1749)

  • He was the son of Sambhaji.
  • He was released by Mughal Emperor Bahadur Shah.
  • He defeated Tarabai in the Battle of Khed (1767).

Balaji Viswanath (1713-1720)

  • In 1713, he became the first Peshwa (PM of Marathas).
  • He began his career as small revenue official and was given the title "Senakarte" (Maker of the Army) by Shahu in 1708.

Baji Rao I (1720-1740)

  • He was the eldest son of Balaji Viswanath.
  • He defeated: Nizam-ul-Mulk and Asaf Jah I (Khan Siddiqi, the first Nizam of Hyderabad).
  • He signed: Treaty of Doraha Sarai with Jai Singh after a victory over a combined force of the Nizam, Awadh, and Rajput states of Jaipur and Rota.
  • In 1737 he raided Delhi.
  • During Baji Rao I's tenure, the concept of the Maratha Confederacy emerged.
  • Son: Balaji Baji Rao.
  • Baji Rao I captured Bassein from Portuguese in 1739.

Balaji Baji Rao (1740-1761)

  • He is also known as Nana Saheb.
  • During his tenure, the 3rd Battle of Panipat was fought between Marathas and Afghans in 1761. Peshwa Sadashivrao Bhau led the Maratha army and Ahmad Shah Abdali from Durrani Empire, led the Afghan forces. The Marathas lost the battle.
  • The 3rd Battle of Panipat is known as one of the deadliest war in the entire world.

Maratha Confederacy

  • Peshwa of Pune
  • Holkar of Indore
  • Gaekwad of Baroda
  • Scindias of Gwalior
  • Bhonsle of Nagpur

Anglo-Maratha Wars

_(1st Anglo-Maratha War content continues on next page)_

1st Anglo-Maratha War: 1775-1782

  • This war began when Raghunath Rao signed Treaty of Purandar (1776) with Britishers to support him to become Peshwa.
  • The Britishers were defeated initially and Treaty of Wadgaon (1779) was signed.
  • Subsequently, Britishers attacked again under the leadership of Warren Hastings and defeated Marathas. Treaty of Salbai (1782) was signed at the end.

2nd Anglo Maratha War: 1803-1805

  • Baji Rao II signed a subsidiary alliance with the British in the form of Treaty of Bassein (1802) which led to the 2nd Anglo-Maratha War. This war was won by British.
  • The 2nd Anglo-Maratha War ended with signing of Treaty of Rajghat (1805) with Holkars.
  • The Treaty of Deogaon signed after Battle of Argaon during 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803) with Bhonsles Dynasty. Cuttack was acquired by Britishers after this war.

3rd Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818)

  • This war is often regarded as "Pindari War".
  • Pindaris were tribal people that supported Marathas during raids.
  • Baji Rao II was captured and sent to Bithoor (Kanpur).
  • Treaty of Mandsaur (1818) signed between the British and the Holkar chief.
  • From 1818, Peshwaship was abolished.
